event_confirmation: Company IR release 2026-10-15 'Coursera to Announce Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results': results 'after the U.S. stock market closes on Thursday, October 29, 2026', call 2:00 p.m. PT / 5:00 p.m. ET. https://investor.coursera.com/news/news-details/2026/Coursera-to-Announce-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx (listed in https://investor.coursera.com/rss/pressrelease.aspx dated Thu, 15 Oct 2026). The vendor Oct 26 date is wrong.
conviction_note: The event is confirmed amc 2026-10-29. The bar is low: the Q3 guide implies about -6% normalized YoY against -1% in Q2. There are buybacks below the $5.66 deal price, a 10.9% holder adding, and upside-paid skew. Against that, this name has sold 5 of its last 7 real prints, including a beat-and-raise in Q2 2026 (-14.7%), and moves on the forward guide. A peer (Skillsoft) cut on accelerating consumer pressure after COUR last spoke. So p_up sits at 51 on an abs move of 16 (+0.32), while the findings sum to +0.70: the sum and the scaled number agree on a slight upside lean, and both are close to a non-result.
bar: Q3 revenue $364-372m and adj EBITDA $52-56m, company guide (Q2 8-K ex.99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001651562/000165156226000059/cour-20260630xexx991.htm). Consensus revenue $368.52m / adj EPS $0.18 (Tiger 2026-10-22, https://www.itiger.com/news/1135204261) and $368.6m / $0.16 (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/COUR/earnings-forecasts). One outlier, Chartmill, shows $375.9m (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/COUR/estimates). Two agreeing sources plus the guide midpoint ($368m) put the bar at about $368.5m. FY26 guide is $1.220-1.245bn revenue, adj EBITDA margin about 14%, Q4 exit margin above 16%. Base-rate note: baseline history row 2025-10-02 is the CFO-transition 8-K (items 2.02/5.02/7.01, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251002508368/en/Coursera-Announces-CFO-Transition/), not a scheduled print. Rebuilt on the 7 real prints: median |move| 12.88%, 5 of 7 down (Q2'26 -14.72 on beat+raise, Q1'26 -11.56 in line, Q4'25 -1.17, Q3'25 -12.88 beat but weak Q4 guide, Q2'25 +36.23, Q1'25 +13.64, Q4'24 -11.69).
positioning_check: Short interest 23,702,312 shares = 10.71% of float, 3.7 days to cover, settlement 2026-10-15, down 6.2% from 25.28m (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/COUR/short-interest/). Elevated, but not the 18-23% squeeze zone. 25-delta skew is -15.79 vol points: upside paid, calls bid over puts. ATM IV is 94.5%, event-implied move 18.88% against a rebuilt historical median of 12.88%. Spot $4.68 is 0.9% above the 52-week low and 45% off the high, -7.7% over 5 days into the print. Holder flow: Baillie Gifford went to 0 shares by 2026-09-30 (13G/A), NEA fell to 4.9% (13G/A event 2026-09-24), and Pale Fire Capital bought on the open market to 10.9%.

findings.finding: The Q3 guide is a low bar. $364-372m (midpoint $368m, consensus $368.5m) against a combined Q3 2025 base of $389.9m (Coursera $194.2m + Udemy $195.7m) implies about -5.6% normalized YoY revenue. That is a sharp deceleration from the -1% normalized decline Coursera disclosed for Q2 2026. Q2 beat consensus by about $5m (+1.7%), so a print at or above the top of the range ($372m, about +1%) is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold. Q2 2026 beat revenue by $5m and EPS by $0.09 with a raised FY guide, and the stock closed -14.72%. Q3 2025 beat and raised, and the stock closed -12.88% on the Q4 guide. Q1 2026 was in line and closed -11.56%.
findings.why_not_priced: The street models the guided $368m and does not quote a normalized-growth comparison. If the market priced a beat, spot would not sit 0.9% above its 52-week low at about 1x book. The guide includes about $10m a quarter of purchase-accounting effects and assumes continued transactional softness, so part of the deceleration is explained, and the finding is inside the company's range.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 comparison bases: Coursera ($194.2m, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1651562/000165156225000056/cour-20250930xshareholde.htm) and Udemy ($195.7m, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1607939/000160793925000138/q32025pressrelease.htm). Same company guide as the bar; no independent demand series.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-09, after Coursera last spoke, peer Skillsoft cut its FY27 revenue guide to $380-390m from $388-406m, citing 'accelerating pressure in the consumer business'. Its enterprise business 'continues to perform as planned'. This is a negative read-through for Udemy's consumer transactional marketplace (Udemy consumer segment -9% in Q3 2025) and for the Q4 implied guide. The FY guide implies Q4 revenue of about $354-387m, midpoint about $370m, flat on Q3, which is the line this stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The forward guide has driven the big down moves: Q3 2025 -12.88% on a disappointing Q4 revenue guide despite a beat, and Q2 2026 -14.72% despite a raised FY guide, on enterprise and normalized-growth concerns.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer cut reads into COUR only through a proxy, and the Q2 shareholder letter already assumed 'transactional softness' and tighter paid marketing. If the market had fully priced a weaker consumer guide, skew would lean to puts; it is -15.8, upside paid.
findings.independence: Udemy consumer segment -9% in Q3 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1607939/000160793925000138/q32025pressrelease.htm). The proxy is Skillsoft's Codecademy-type consumer business, not COUR's own number. Against it, Coursera's own consumer subscription revenue grew 19% in Q2.

findings.finding: Enterprise skills demand at peers was stable to firm in the September quarter. Pearson's 9-month update (2026-10-22) shows Enterprise Learning & Skills +6% in Q3 and +7% for 9M. Skillsoft's enterprise business is 'performing as planned'. COUR's own enterprise NRR fell to 91% in Q2, with enterprise customers -2%, so the peer read only argues against a further sharp enterprise deterioration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Enterprise weakness (NRR drop, customer pullback) was cited for the Q2 2026 -14.72% and the Q3 2025 -12.88% reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: It came out a week before the print and is a different-company series; previews quote only the guide. It is a proxy, so small.
findings.independence: Skillsoft enterprise commentary in the same 2026-09-09 release used for finding 2 (shared document for the enterprise half).

findings.finding: The share count fell from 274.5m (2026-06-30) to 264.4m (2026-07-29, 10-Q cover), about 10m shares or 3.7% retired in July alone, at about $5 a share against the $5.66 Udemy deal price. About $360m of the $500m authorization remains, against roughly $1bn of cash and securities and a market cap of about $1.24bn. The Q3 weighted share guidance (267m basic) excludes buybacks after July 28, so continued buying at $4.6-5.1 would show up in the print as lower share count and EPS upside against the $0.16-0.18 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $500m program was announced in May and buybacks were disclosed with Q2. The stock still fell 14.72% on that print, so buybacks alone have not carried a reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 repurchase volume is not public until the release. If the market expected heavy repurchase at these prices, a stock with net cash near three-quarters of its market cap would not trade at its 52-week low. Integration cash costs (about $60m in H2) and the $100m LearnVector investment compete for the same cash.
findings.independence: Q2 8-K: about $140m repurchased through 2026-07-28 against $90.3m in Q2 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001651562/000165156226000059/cour-20260630xexx991.htm). Same company, different document.

findings.finding: Pale Fire Capital (ex-Udemy holder) bought 1,332,742 shares at $5.06 on 2026-09-25 and 1,000,000 at $4.61 on 2026-09-29, reaching 28.8m shares or 10.9% (Form 4 / 13G/A, passive certification). In the same window long-only Baillie Gifford exited to 0 (event 2026-09-30) and NEA fell to 4.9% (event 2026-09-24). Holder supply has been rotating from exiting funds to a strategic accumulator at about these prices.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print with a comparable holder event.
findings.why_not_priced: The filings are public and the stock is lower since, at $4.68, so this is mostly priced. It matters as supply: two exiting holders' selling appears complete per their filings.

findings.finding: Short interest is 23.7m shares, 10.71% of float, 3.7 days to cover (2026-10-15), with call-side skew of -15.8 vol points. The stock enters the print 0.9% off its 52-week low and -7.7% over 5 days, so a non-negative print has a short-covering mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2025 (+36.23%) is the one large squeeze-like upside in the history. The other 5 of 7 real prints fell.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the thing to beat rather than an edge. At 10.7% this is not a crowded short. It only conditions the reaction to a good print.
findings.independence: Baseline skew -15.79 and the 18.88% event-implied move (sealed baseline).

findings.finding: AltIndex reports 53.5m coursera.org monthly visits as of 2026-09-15, +4.6% month on month and +20% over three months, against about 44.6m in mid-June. This is a weak, seasonal (back-to-school) proxy for consumer funnel health in the quarter, with no year-on-year comparison available.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history linking traffic to reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Third-party estimate, not aggregated by previews. It is a proxy with no YoY figure, so it is tiny.
findings.independence: none. A 2025 Similarweb study showed YoY traffic declines at Coursera and Udemy tied to AI chatbots (https://ppc.land/ai-chatbots-drive-traffic-decline-for-major-online-course-platforms/), which cuts the other way.

outside_window.finding: Project Helix, the AI-native enterprise platform announced 2026-09-09, is expected to be broadly available in the first half of 2027. It has no revenue in the window.
The full $115m synergy run-rate is targeted before end-2027; only part of the at-least-$85m run-rate lands in 2026 reported results.

searched_and_found_nothing: Event date: confirmed by the company's 2026-10-15 release; the vendor Oct 26 estimate is wrong.
EDGAR 8-K flow since Q2: only the 2026-09-21 Chief Legal Officer transition (5.02/7.01). No guidance, no pre-announcement, no new restructuring 8-K after the 2026-07-06 item 2.05.
Insider Form 4s: one CEO 10b5-1 sale of 10,308 shares at $5.11 (2026-10-01) and an RSU grant to the new CLO. Nothing material.
Goodwill impairment risk: goodwill only $182.7m and market cap (~$1.24bn) above June 30 book equity of $1,167m, so no visible trigger.
Analyst actions in October 2026: none found. Tiger's 10-22 summary lists BMO, Needham and William Blair at Buy, with no fresh downgrades.
Takeover or activist chatter: none in 2026 beyond Pale Fire's passive 13G.
Udemy instructor and community forums: anecdotal complaints only, no dated quantified data.
Q2 2026 call commentary on Q3 seasonality: none found beyond the shareholder letter.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Udemy instructors report falling course earnings after the merger; claim that Udemy cut the subscription revenue share from 25% toward 15%
rejected_candidates.detail: Forum anecdotes and a secondary statistics page (skillademia.com) with no dated, quantified company figure.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Chartmill Q3 revenue consensus of $375.89m (higher bar)
rejected_candidates.detail: Outside the company guide range of $364-372m; two other sources (Tiger 10-22, Benzinga) agree on $368.5-368.6m.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Baseline history row 2025-10-02 (-8.56%) used as an earnings reaction
rejected_candidates.detail: That 8-K was the CFO-transition release, not the Q3 2025 print (reported 2025-10-23). It was excluded from the base rate.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly upward with the upside-paid skew (-15.8) and against the 5-of-7-down reaction history. The one negative, the Skillsoft consumer read-through on the guide line, is the line this name has actually traded on, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: L1 (verified fact is not a reaction) and L6 (inside the guided range): low-bar beat finding cut from +0.8 to +0.4, because this name sold a beat-and-raise for -14.7%.
L7 (sign against strong skew): Skillsoft consumer read-through negative cut from -1.5 to -1.0, because skew is -15.8 upside paid and short interest is 10.7%.
L1: buyback finding cut from +0.8 to +0.6, because the announced program did not prevent the Q2 selloff.
L5 and L7 (positioning is context, proxies small): Pale Fire holder finding +0.3 to +0.2, short interest finding +0.4 to +0.2, traffic proxy +0.2 to +0.1.
Lessons file note on untrustworthy history: base rate rebuilt on 7 real prints (dropped the 2025-10-02 CFO 8-K), median 12.88%. abs_move 16 and p_up 51 unchanged.
